## CI comes from one repository

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- Every package's workflows are thin callers into 22 reusable workflows in
  one `.github` repository, as SciML does it
- Each caller pins the reusable workflow to a commit SHA
- `EpiAwarePackageTools.jl` writes those callers and overwrites them every
  Monday
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
```yaml
# MANAGED by EpiAwarePackageTools.scaffold
# — do not edit by hand.
name: Test

jobs:
  test:
    uses: EpiAware/.github/.github/workflows/tests.yml@d024dc6
```

::: {.attribution}
`.github/workflows/test.yaml` in `ComposableTuringIDModels.jl`, SHA
abridged, read 2026-08-12 · 22 of the 23 workflows in
[EpiAware/.github](https://github.com/EpiAware/.github) declare
`workflow_call`, counted from the contents API 2026-08-13 ·
`template-sync.yaml` runs Monday 04:00 UTC.
:::
:::
::::

## One package writes the tooling in the others

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- `scaffold` writes the tooling into a package once. `update` re-applies it
  and reports drift
- 78 template files, most of them force-managed, so an edited file comes
  back on the next sync
- Over 10,000 lines of Julia hold ten of the eleven packages rigid

::: {.callout-important}
We should probably have built this on `BestieTemplate.jl`'s Copier template
rather than writing our own scaffolder.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
```julia
using EpiAwarePackageTools

scaffold(pkgdir(MyPackage))

# again on every sync
EpiAwarePackageTools.update(pkgdir(MyPackage))
```

::: {.attribution}
`src/` and `templates/` in
[EpiAwarePackageTools.jl](https://github.com/EpiAware/EpiAwarePackageTools.jl),
counted at commit `427d4f5` on `main`, 2026-08-12 · ten of the eleven Julia
packages carry `template-sync.yaml` on `main`, checked through the contents
API 2026-08-12 ·
[BestieTemplate.jl](https://github.com/JuliaBesties/BestieTemplate.jl) and
[PkgTemplates.jl](https://github.com/JuliaCI/PkgTemplates.jl).
:::
:::
::::

## R has a stack of checks. Julia has Aqua, and we went past it

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- In R a package arrives with a definition of good already attached.
  `R CMD check`, CRAN policy, rOpenSci review
- In Julia you get `Aqua`, and after that you decide. We decided on nine
  checks that run in every package
- JET is one of the nine. Benchmarks and the per-backend AD tests run
  alongside them
- All of it runs in CI
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
```julia
@testitem "Quality: Aqua"
@testitem "Quality: ExplicitImports"
@testitem "Quality: import centralisation"
@testitem "Quality: docstring format"
@testitem "Quality: README sections"
@testitem "Quality: doctest"
@testitem "Quality: formatting"
@testitem "Quality: linting (JET)"
@testitem "Quality: extension ambiguities"
```

::: {.attribution}
`templates/test/package/quality.jl` in `EpiAwarePackageTools.jl`, written
into each adopting package and overwritten on every sync, read 2026-08-12.
:::
:::
::::

## Nothing in Julia checks the packages downstream of you

- CRAN policy asks you to check that packages depending on yours still pass
  `R CMD check` before you update. Julia has no equivalent
- SciML runs downstream CI against two packages it does not own
- Our scaffold writes a downstream job into all ten packages, run by a label
  on a pull request. In all ten the list of downstreams is empty
- Every package also tests against its lowest allowed dependency versions

::: {.attribution}
[CRAN Repository Policy](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html),
read 2026-08-12 · `downstream.yaml` and the `downgrade-compat` job read
through the contents API across the ten packages that carry them,
2026-08-12 · SciML's `Downstream.yml` in `OrdinaryDiffEq.jl` runs
`ProbNumDiffEq.jl` and `PositiveIntegrators.jl`, read 2026-08-10.
:::
